To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intervention research can have a significant impact on policy and practice, but this is not inevitable, and the impact of a research project is dependent on a number of factors, some of which can be controlled and others which can not be controlled by researchers.

intervention research can achieve the greatest impact on policy and practice if it is designed and conducted in partnership with policy and practice end users and uses a range of dissemination strategies to communicate findings.

intervention research can have policy and practice impacts, but these impacts are not guaranteed and depend on a number of factors, some within the researchers' control and others outside the researchers' control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: what is the impact of applied research in health promotion on policy and practice?
understanding the factors that facilitate and impede the use of research findings by health policy makers and practitioners.
the use of evidence to inform policy making and the factors that influence the uptake of evidence by policy makers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intervention research projects that are well designed and executed and that engage with policy and practice stakeholders from the outset can be effective in informing policy and practice.

the impacts of intervention research are mediated by a number of complex and inter-related factors, including the nature of the intervention, leadership and champions, research quality, effective partnerships, dissemination strategies used and contextual factors.
this research has provided new insights into the mechanisms and conditions that mediate impacts of intervention research, which should be of value to researchers, policy makers and practitioners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

intervention research can be an important tool for influencing real world policy and programs if the right research questions are being asked and the right people are being involved in the research process.

the findings from the study highlight that the most effective way to influence policy and practice is to work closely with end users from the beginning of research projects, to ensure that the research addresses proximal needs of policy and practice.

the research was used to inform policy development and practice, and the factors that contributed to its use included: i) the nature of the intervention, ii) leadership and championing, iii) research quality, iv) effective partnerships, v) dissemination strategies, vi) contextual influences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intervention research is not an end in itself, rather a means to an end.
the most important factor in determining the use of research in practice is the quality of the research, and the second most important factor is how the research is presented.
the research community needs to be aware of the importance of dissemination strategies and that dissemination should be considered a core component of intervention research.
